summary: Phase 1 billing/tax/commission rules — all 7 scenarios covered. 10/10 tests PASSED. HTTP /api/bookings/quote returns the exact expected numbers for Patna (schedule 442.86 total, emergency 598.26 total). Rate-card commission applies only to labour (+Min Labour Charge fallback). Additional-work _recompute_additional uses platform_pct=(100-partner_pct), no platform_fee, GST only on labour commission. Merchant city-wise commission (Patna 4%/2%) correctly OVERRIDES category (5%/3%) via CommissionEngine.split. Partner invoice breakdown strips platform_fee + GST (tax=0, platform_fee not in additional_charges) while customer breakdown keeps them. Regression: normal booking still distributes 80/20 with pass_through=0, distributed==service_net.
critical_code_review_comments: booking_controller._build_booking (line ~631) mutates svc['base_price'] by adding min_labour but DOES NOT clear/update discounted_price. For a standard (non-custom) service this would cause selling_price() to still return the smaller discounted price, silently losing the labour-charge addition. Currently safe only because the branch is gated to svc.get('is_custom') AND custom services are created with discounted_price=0 (line 226). Add an explicit comment or also set svc['discounted_price']=0 defensively.

engines.CommissionEngine._cm reads commission block from booking.commission_config directly, but booking_controller stores it under commission_config['commission']. compute_split/settle both correctly use booking.get('commission_config') or settings which is then _cm'd — the fallback keys inside _cm reference legacy flat keys from settings, so a snapshot like {'commission': {...}} works, but a snapshot that FORGOT the 'commission' sub-key would silently fall through to legacy constants (60/32/5/3). Consider validating ccfg contains the 'commission' subdoc on write.

Partner-facing build_breakdown surfaces customer_only_charges separately but strip_platform_fees_breakdown recomputes tax=0 hardcoded; if a future change puts non-platform-only GST on the service side it would be wiped for partners. Acceptable today (GST only on commission + platform fee), but worth asserting invariant.
